reasoning: Despite high fidelity scores (composite 0.8967) and strong programmatic text recall (0.98), the document exhibits structural defects that explicitly block auto-approval. Running headers, footers, and page numbers were retained in the HTML output. Furthermore, a single 38-page continuous table was split into 19 separate tables, causing subsequent tables to lose column headers and breaking accessibility.

In the HTML output, this bold formatting has been entirely stripped, rendering all headers and category titles as plain text, which severely impacts the visual hierarchy and distinctnes

concerns.analysis: header_footer_count=7. Running headers/footers/page numbers should be stripped during PDF-to-HTML conversion.

The source document is a single 38-page continuous table. The pipeline improperly split this single table into 19 separate table objects (one per every pair of pages). Because the PDF only contains column headers (Section, Part Number, Description, Previous Price, 2025 Price) on the first page, splitting the table means tables 2 through 19 in the JSON have no column headers. This completely breaks data association for screen reader users trying to read the vast majority of the document. Addition
concerns.source_pdf_quote: A continuous table grid spanning 38 pages, with column headers 'Section | Part Number | Description | Previous Price | 2025 Price' only at the top of page 1.
concerns.output_quote: The output contains separate 'type: table' objects on pages 1, 3, 5, 7, etc. The table on JSON page 3 starts directly with data ('121805') at row_start: 0 with no headers.

action_items: Remove retained page numbers and running headers/footers from the HTML.
Reunify the split tables or ensure column headers are properly repeated/associated for each section of the table.
Change the single spanning first row of the table to a <caption> element instead of a header row.
Restore bold formatting to headers and category titles to preserve visual hierarchy.
